items.title: std::http `Request` has no peer address - kolt's sign-in throttle reads it through a JS binding native refuses
items.body: The last behaviour-dropping workaround in kolt's native server build (W1 in sweeps/order58/native-m1-report.md). Kolt reads `request.socket.remoteAddress` through an app binding; natively `peer_address` returns an empty string, so every client shares one sign-in throttle unless KOLT_TRUST_PROXY=1. Fix: `Request::peer_address(self): Option<str>` (or `remote_address`) in std on both backends - node's `socket.remoteAddress`, the native accept's peer. This is ruling S2's first door (general binding moves into std); the two-arm `[extern(js = .., rust = ..)]` is not needed for it. Size S. Closes M1's build half with zero workarounds.

items.title: Native: indexing through a `Shared` read in a `for` condition moves a `str` parameter inside the loop (rustc E0382)
items.body: Repro: sweeps/order58/repros/loop-cond-move/main.vl - prints 2 on JS, rustc refuses the native emit with E0382 (use of moved value). A `str` parameter passed to a method inside a loop whose condition indexes through a `Shared` read is moved, not cloned, on the second turn. Kolt does not hit it today. Size S.

items.title: Building a single file with `--backend rust` writes a stray `<file>.css` next to the source
items.body: A native single-file build leaves `<file>.css` beside the source file. The native backend has no use for the stylesheet output on a server program; it should not be written (or should go to the output directory). Size XS.
